svg.text: PAPEL Sequence Diagram: a paper from Submit to published

Every message is a real call. The order is the design: Drive is asked about before anything is stored, every file is up before the transaction opens, and nothing after the commit may report a failure.
Solid arrowhead: a call. Dashed open arrowhead: a return. alt / loop frames are the handler's own branches.
2. The Subject Adviser reviews, and forwards
3. The Research Coordinator publishes. This is the last step.
for each declared format: imrad, full, or other
4. at least 5 keywords, the section scope, other_name_problem()
8. ok | unset | not_found | not_folder | trashed | read_only | unknown
13. unlink the staging copy: Drive holds the paper now
16. INSERT paper_manuscripts, one row per format (and the mirror columns)
17. INSERT supporting_documents: the four named rows and the student's own
20. delete_from_gdrive() for every file this request made
22. creator_of(student) : the Subject Adviser who made the account
27. POST action=approve, with the review checklist
32. set_status(paper, 'draft'); the feedback stays on the workflow row
33. purge_paper_drive_files(paper): both files go, so the student attaches them again
35. guard: the paper really is in pending_admin or pending_admin_l1
38. analytics.time_to_approval: upload_date to now, in days
40. the paper is in the public repository, and readable by anyone
Nothing after the commit may report a failed upload. The paper is filed by then, so the tail (deleting the files the new ones replaced,
telling the adviser) sits in a try of its own: a failure there is logged against a reference and the student is still told their paper was
submitted. It used to answer "Upload failed" for a paper that was in fact filed, which invites filing it twice.
A draft holds no PDF, on this server or on Drive. save_draft takes no $_FILES at all, so a student returning to a draft attaches the files
again and the prompt only lists the names they had used. Submitting from a draft updates that row rather than adding a second copy,
which is what keeps a returned paper's feedback and approval history attached to it.
The chain ends here. The Head of Academic Programs and the Director read what comes out of it and do not approve. A paper uploaded by
a member of staff skips both steps: student_upload_ai.php files it as approved at once. Returning a paper at either step sets it back to draft,
so draft means either "never submitted" or "returned", and the approval_workflow rows are what tell them apart.
